summary.headline: Amara Raja Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose ~24% to ~INR4,215 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 9.6% on input costs and strategic spends.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 24% to roughly INR4,215 crore, with lead acid up about 22% and new energy up more than 70% to about INR209 crore. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 10.1% and consolidated 9.6%, hit by raw material inflation (alloy, sulfuric acid, poly), brand spends including IPL, Amaron Assist pilot, Factory of the Future costs and higher warranty provisions. Management took ~3% price hikes in June with a further 2-3% planned in the current month, but B2B pass-through lags. Automotive international volumes fell about 20% on Middle East disruption, and management expects recovery in subsequent quarters.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management attributes ~0.9pp hit to strategic spends
~0.5pp lower, mainly new energy Giga 1 and BESS costs
elevated due to tubular season and inverter/HUPS trading
part of FY27 plan of ~INR1,700 crore

segments.name: Automotive lead acid (aftermarket & OEM)
segments.commentary: Aftermarket 4W and 2W volumes up ~15% YoY; OEM volumes up ~24% in 4W and >35% in 2W. Tubular plant ran at 100% capacity.

segments.name: Automotive international
segments.commentary: Revenue degrew ~20% YoY on ~20% volume drop, mainly lower Middle East shipments due to costly alternative sea routes.

segments.name: Industrial lead acid
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~2% YoY; UPS volumes up ~10%, telecom lead acid degrowing as telecom shifts to lithium-ion. Railways and power control growing 5-6%.

segments.name: Home energy
segments.commentary: Growth of more than 60% in tubular batteries and home EPS.

segments.name: New energy (lithium-ion packs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR209 crore, up >70%; EV and telecom pack volumes each up >50% YoY. Lithium-ion telecom volumes up ~50%, combined telecom share held above 60%.

guidance_outlook: Additional 2-3% price increases across product segments in the current month (August); B2B pass-through expected to lag, with most recovery likely in Q2 or next quarter.
Other expenses (brand promotion, Amaron Assist, Factory of the Future) expected to normalise over next couple of quarters; freight and warranty costs may recur if fuel and raw material costs persist.
Lead acid revenue growth guided at 9-10% over the medium term (volume-led, industry-level estimate, not formal guidance); 2W aftermarket lower double digits, 4W slightly lower.
FY27 capex of ~INR1,700 crore, of which ~INR1,300 crore for new energy; Giga 1 expected to commercialise in H1 FY28.
BESS 10 GWh factory: initial capex INR250-300 crore; management sees ~5 GWh utilisation within 6-7 months of completion. Working capital cycle of 90-100 days cited as achievable.
R&D spend on cell development of ~INR100-150 crore expected this year.
E Positive research facility expected to start operations in the current quarter; 2 GWh NMC line equipment due for delivery in Q3.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at ~INR1,700 crore (~INR1,300 crore new energy); ~INR450 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Giga 1 cell plant expected to commercialise in H1 FY28; 2 GWh NMC line equipment due in Q3 FY27.
10 GWh LFP BESS factory on track; initial outlay INR250-300 crore; operating margin guided at roughly 5-8%.
Customer qualification plant with multi-form, multi-chemistry capability inaugurated in July 2026; producing 2170 NMC B-samples.
Tubular plant ran at 100% utilisation in Q1; battery breaking (recycling) operations still in trial production.

Long-term 16 GWh target from earlier strategy now under review; management says timing and capacity can change with demand and product mix; strategic share goal of 15-20% of lithium cell potential retained.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation in poly, sulfuric acid and tin/alloys; ~3% price hike taken in June 2026 did not fully offset cost increase.
Warranty provisions raised due to higher raw material costs, applied to the entire unexpired population.
Chinese competition: management estimates a 15-20% price disadvantage versus China for lithium cells; expects 3-4 cell players in India.
Telecom lead acid migrating to lithium-ion; combined telecom share above 60%.
BESS demand visibility from EPC players for power generation projects in India; export opportunities flagged.
Recycling economics: scrap purchase and reprocessing costs roughly equal to or above LME lead currently.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken in Q1 and have cost pressures been recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% taken in Q1 and a further 2-3% in August; not fully offsetting raw material rises, with poly, sulfuric acid and tin still trending up. B2B hikes delayed, expected to be recovered by Q2 or next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are other expenses non-recurring, and what is the BESS economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand and Amaron Assist costs to normalise over a couple of quarters; warranty and freight may recur. BESS: INR250-300 crore capex for 10 GWh, LFP-based, operating margin around 5-8% and asset turns higher than pack business.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the ~0.9% margin hit and how other expenses will trend.
qa_highlights.answer: Hit is from brand promotion, Amaron Assist pilot and Factory of the Future (capitalisation not allowed for throughput initiatives); also warranty and freight. Other expenses should trend lower once projects complete, but freight and warranty stay elevated while input costs are high.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16 GWh lithium plan still on track after the Gotion setback?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity milestones can change with demand; the 15-20% market share strategy holds. ESS cells may be prioritised over standard EV cells. NMC technology gap de-risked by in-house improvements; no broad China tech tie-up feasible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lead acid growth outlook and is the price hike volume-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term lead acid revenue growth of 9-10% is an industry-level estimate, mainly volume-led. Aftermarket growth moderating from high base; 2W lower double digits, 4W slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: How will the holding company fund new energy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial risk capital of ~INR2,500 crore to complete five facilities; holding company cash generation of INR700-800 crore post-tax and post-dividend. Future debt-to-equity decisions to be made per business case.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation in poly, sulfuric acid and tin/alloys may persist; B2B price hikes lag, so Q2 margin recovery depends on whether the ~2-3% August hike sticks.
Warranty provisions and freight costs may recur next quarter if fuel and raw material prices stay high.
Automotive international volumes (Middle East) down ~20%; recovery depends on geopolitical developments and sea-route freight costs.

BESS ramp-up: management expects ~5 GWh utilisation within 6-7 months of completion, but said it is not a firm order-backed commitment; margin and asset-turn figures were given as ranges and remain unconfirmed.
Lithium-ion scale-up: 16 GWh target under review, cathode dependence on China, 15-20% price disadvantage versus Chinese cells, and no broad China technology tie-up possible.
Holding company funding: ~INR2,500 crore initial risk capital, ~INR700-800 crore annual post-tax, post-dividend cash generation; future debt-to-equity policy not yet set.
key_quotes: So if the current prices were to stay where they are, this might be sufficient.
So I don't think I can give you a 100% sure number at this point of time, but if I were to give an estimate, a 90 day to 100-day kind of a cash conversion cycle is not impossible to achieve.
It's not that I will build the capacity irrespective of what demand signals that I am getting and which cells that are being required by the customers.

But I wouldn't want to put a number at this point of time because I need to see each of these business cases and accordingly decide whether a leverage is good or should I look at some other options for funding this kind of expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on lead acid volumes, aftermarket and OEM demand, and the Q2 price recovery, but cautious on margins, B2B pass-through and international shipments. Evasive on specifics for BESS asset turns, warranty provisioning for lithium packs, and the revised 16 GWh capacity path, repeatedly deferring numbers until pilots or plant runs are complete.
